claims.statement: Tom Allen and George Rooke were matched to fight for the championship of America and $1,000 a side, within fifty miles of Detroit, on 15 July 1875.
claims.excerpt: fifty miles of Detroit, on the 15th of July

claims.statement: Harry Hill returned the $3,000 stakes from the first match and kept $1,000 of Allen's money to post for the new contest.
claims.excerpt: Harry Hill retains $1,000 of Allen’s money to post on the coming contest

claims.statement: Allen told the Republican the news of the new arrangements was new to him, and that Harry Hill was authorized to act for him.
claims.excerpt: the information was new to him; that ’Arry ’Ill was duly authorized to act for him

claims.statement: Tom Allen was found at his establishment, Tom Allen's Free and Easy, in the company of sporting men.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen’s Free and Easy’’ the champion himself was

claims.statement: Tom Allen was living in St. Louis in June 1875.
claims.excerpt: whose residence among us has made our city the headquarters

fights.stakes: $1,000 a side, and the championship of America
fights.excerpt: fifty miles of Detroit, on the 15th of July
fights.notes: Planned date from a New York telegram dated 28 June 1875; Rooke chooses the ground. The article does not say whether it was fought.

notes: Telegram from New York plus a short interview with Allen; the interview is reported in paraphrase, no direct quotes.
